pull.title: KAFKA-15677: Require RE2/J syntax for new/changed client-metrics match patterns
pull.body:
**What**
KIP-714's client-metrics match config patterns are now validated with RE2/J syntax when a subscription's match value is new or has actually changed. A pre-existing subscription whose match pattern only compiles under java.util.regex is still compiled successfully, via a deprecated, temporary fallback that logs a warning.. The fallback will be removed in Apache Kafka 5.0.

**Why**
RE2/J guarantees linear-time matching, which matters here because match patterns are evaluated against client-supplied strings.

The switch needed care because RE2/J supports only a subset of regexes that java.util.regex supported and we wanted to ensure that existing match patterns compile even if they are not part of that subset.

Reviewers: Apoorv Mittal <apoorvmittal10@gmail.com>, Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>

review_comments.body: I suppose it's for already configured client subscriptions but I was wondering do we need to keep supporting or start porting them itself with a log message.

To support backward compatibility, I have gone ahead with the following behaviour - If user updates an existing subscription, without updating the "match" field, the user should not get an error if any of the patterns is not supported in RE2. This is why we need the old configs of the subscription, to check if "match" field was changed in the new config. If yes, we compile the new patterns using RE2, if not, we skip it.

review_comments.body:
> Can you please provide me example when this will be used i.e. scenario?

This is used in the fallback path of `compileLenient`. We first try to compile the pattern using RE2, if it does not succeed we try using the existing library. If it succeeds, we log a warning. `compileLenient` gets called in two flows:

1. When a config is altered and the change is propagated to the brokers, all brokers call it when updating their subscriptions.
2. When a broker rebuilds its state using the metadata log (for eg. during startup).
Happy to hear your thoughts if you feel a different behaviour would be more suitable.

review_comments.body: Yes, that's right. My thinking is - once someone's already touching a subscription's match config, it's reasonable to ask them to bring the whole list up to RE2/J compliance in the same request, rather than only checking the specific entry they added.

It is weird that we are lenient only for regex. The method validateConfigs still validates other configs. If we trust the configs from the metadata, the whole validateConfigs should be skipped.

@apoorvmittal10 @ojasvajain @AndrewJSchofield WDYT?

`updateSubscription` is called in two scenarios  - when a live config is altered and propagated to the brokers, and when a broker replays the metadata logs. For the first case, removing the validate call should be fine as we would have run the same validation on controller during "alter".

The second case needs more thought for when a broker is restarted with a new version. The validate call above does provide a way to check whether existing subscriptions still follow the latest rules, since it's the same method the controller calls during alter. But whenever we introduce a backward-incompatible change to a subscription field in a minor version (e.g. narrowing the interval range, or adding a mandatory field), we'd need to skip this check for that field via some workaround and validate it with a fallback instead. When we move to the next major version, we'd want to remove the fallback and reinstate the validate call, so all subscriptions are required to follow the new rules.

For our case of making the regex stricter, the fallback validation already happens in updateClientSubscription, so this validate call adds no value here and can be removed. In Apache Kafka 5.0, we can simply drop the fallback without reinstating this validate call. If we ever need to make a different backward-incompatible change to the subscription, we can revisit this then.
Please open a blocker ticket for 5.0.0 for removing this fallback, and reference it in the comment :)
yes, I prefer removing the validation from this path. BTW, I guess removing the check will break some tests
Addessed this in a5b37bac7102d7604aac7b5ad7c9838eadc1ae7e. There was a test case that relied on the validate() call, I have modified its expectations.
I had initially tried to keep it same as how it was before my changes. I have now added legacyException as cause.

+  @Test
+  def testUnchangedMatchClientMetricsConfig(): Unit = {
+    // A pre-existing match pattern that is invalid under RE2/J must not be rejected just
+    // because an unrelated config on the same resource is being changed.
+    val oldConfig = new util.TreeMap[String, String]()
+    oldConfig.put(ClientMetricsConfigs.MATCH_CONFIG, "client_id=(a)\\1")
+
+    val newConfig = new util.TreeMap[String, String]()
+    newConfig.put(ClientMetricsConfigs.MATCH_CONFIG, "client_id=(a)\\1")
+    newConfig.put(ClientMetricsConfigs.INTERVAL_MS_CONFIG, "60000")
+
+    validator.validate(new ConfigResource(CLIENT_METRICS, "subscription-1"), newConfig, oldConfig)
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  def testChangedMatchClientMetricsConfig(): Unit = {
+    // Changing an already-persisted match pattern to a different, illegal one is a
+    // genuine change, so it must still be rejected.
+    val oldConfig = new util.TreeMap[String, String]()
+    oldConfig.put(ClientMetricsConfigs.MATCH_CONFIG, "client_id=(a)\\1")
+
+    val newConfig = new util.TreeMap[String, String]()
+    newConfig.put(ClientMetricsConfigs.MATCH_CONFIG, "client_software_version=(\\d+)\\.\\1")
+
+    assertThrows(classOf[InvalidConfigurationException], () => validator.validate(
+      new ConfigResource(CLIENT_METRICS, "subscription-1"), newConfig, oldConfig))
+  }
+

+## Upgrading to 4.5.0
+
+### Upgrading Servers to 4.5.0 from any version 3.3.x through 4.4.0
+
+### Notable changes in 4.5.0
+
+  * Client metrics subscription (KIP-714) `match` config patterns are now required to be valid RE2/J syntax when creating a subscription or changing its `match` value. A pre-existing `match` pattern that only compiles under java.util.regex (e.g. one relying on backreferences or lookaround) is still matched via a deprecated fallback, which logs a warning on every broker that loads it. This fallback will be removed in Kafka 5.0, so such patterns should be migrated to valid RE2/J syntax before then. For further details, please refer to [KAFKA-15677](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-15677).
+
